ai.literal: As rumor arises, precious life persists; that, many do not know, by good fortune.
ai.translation: My precious life survives only because this rumor of our love arises; fortunately, the many who gossip do not realize this.
ai.modern: அலர் (பழிச்சொல்) எழுவதால் என்னுடைய அரிய உயிர் நிலைத்து நிற்கிறது; அதனைப் பலர் அறியவில்லை, அது என் நல்வாய்ப்பே ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the heroine speaks of how the public rumor (alar) about her secret love actually sustains her life during separation. The gossip of the townspeople serves as a constant validation of her relationship, giving her the strength to endure the pain of absence. Ironically, those who spread the rumor do so to slander her, unaware that their gossip acts as a life-saving medicine. She considers this ignorance of theirs to be her own good fortune, as they would otherwise stop gossiping and she would lose her will to live.

ai.literal: Flower resembling eye-she preciousness not-knowing, gossip to-me gave this town.
ai.translation: Without understanding how precious and difficult to attain my flower-eyed beloved is, this town has gifted me with public gossip.
ai.modern: மலர் போன்ற கண்களை உடையவளின் அருமையை உணராமல், இந்த ஊரார் எங்களுக்கு அலரை (பழிச்சொல்லை) பரிசாகத் தந்துள்ளனர்.
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the lover speaks about the rumors spreading in the town regarding his secret love. He notes that the townspeople do not comprehend the preciousness (அருமை) of his beloved, whose eyes are like flowers (மலரன்ன கண்ணாள்), nor do they understand how difficult she is to attain. Instead of being sympathetic, this town (இவ்வூர்) has simply gifted him with public gossip (அலர்). Though spoken with a touch of irony, this gossip ultimately aids the lover by bringing his secret love into the open, paving the way for marriage.

ai.literal: Will it not befit, the gossip known to the town? That has the nature of having obtained [him] without actually obtaining [him].
ai.translation: Will not the gossip known to the entire town work in my favor? It has the unique nature of making me feel as if I have attained my lover, even before I have actually won him.
ai.modern: ஊரார் அறிந்த இந்த அலர் (வதந்தி) எனக்கு நன்மை செய்யாதோ? என் காதலனை இன்னும் அடையப் பெறாத நிலையிலும், அவனை அடைந்துவிட்டது போன்ற இன்பத்தைத் தரும் தன்மையுடையது அது.
ai.explanation: The heroine reflects on the public gossip spreading through the town regarding her secret love affair. Instead of being distressed by the rumors, she welcomes them. She explains that the gossip has a wonderful effect: it makes her feel as though she has already united with her lover, even before their formal marriage. The key words 'பெறாஅது' (without obtaining) and 'பெற்றன்ன' (as if obtained) highlight this sweet paradox where public exposure solidifies their bond in her heart.

ai.literal: By public gossip, sustained is love; that if not present, shrinking-like nature losing.
ai.translation: My love is sustained and thrives because of public gossip; without that gossip, it would lose its nature and fade away.
ai.modern: ஊராரின் அலர் பேச்சால் என் காமம் வளர்கிறது; அந்த அலர் பேச்சு இல்லாவிட்டால், அது தன் தன்மையை இழந்து சுருங்கிப் போய்விடும்.
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the heroine explains how public gossip ('கவ்வை') about her secret love actually acts as a nutrient that keeps her love alive and thriving ('கவ்விது'). She asserts that if there were no such gossip ('அதுவின்றேல்'), her love would lose its vibrant quality ('தன்மை இழந்து') and wither away. The word 'தவ்' is an imitative word representing shrinking or fading. Thus, rather than destroying their bond, the public talk serves to intensify and sustain their mutual passion.

ai.literal: With every intoxication, drinking liquor is like desiring; love, every time it becomes public, is sweet.
ai.translation: Just as drinking liquor is desired more and more as one's intoxication grows, so does love become sweeter and sweeter each time it is revealed to the public.
ai.modern: மதுவினால் மயக்கம் அதிகமாகும் போதெல்லாம் மேலும் மது குடிக்க விரும்புவதைப் போல, காமம் பிறருக்குத் தெரியவரும் போதெல்லாம் மேலும் இன்பம் தருகிறது.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares the nature of secret love to the addiction of drinking liquor. Normally, lovers might fear their secret affair being exposed to the town, but here they find that public gossip only intensifies their passion. The key word 'களித்தொறும்' means 'with every increasing intoxication', and 'வெளிப்படுந்தொறும்' means 'with every public revelation'. Just as an intoxicated person craves more alcohol with every sip, the lovers find their mutual desire growing sweeter and more irresistible every time their love is talked about.

ai.literal: That which was seen was indeed only one day; the public rumor indeed is like the snake seizing the moon.
ai.translation: Our meeting was but for a single day; yet the public gossip about it has spread instantly, like the eclipse of the moon seized by the serpent.
ai.modern: நாங்கள் ஒருவரை ஒருவர் பார்த்தது ஒரு நாள் மட்டுமே; ஆனால் எங்களைப் பற்றிய வதந்தி, பாம்பானது சந்திரனைப் பிடித்துக் கொண்ட கிரகணத்தைப் போல எங்கும் பரவிவிட்டது.
ai.explanation: The heroine laments how quickly and widely the town has begun to gossip about her secret love. She points out that she and her lover met for only a single day ('கண்டது ஒருநாள்'). Yet, the resulting public rumor ('அலர்') has spread instantly to everyone, just like a lunar eclipse ('திங்களைப் பாம்புகொண்டற்று') where a serpent is believed to seize the moon, drawing the attention of the entire world. The contrast between the brief, private meeting and the massive, public gossip highlights her distress.

ai.literal: Townspeople's gossip becoming manure, mother's words becoming water, grows this disease.
ai.translation: With the townspeople's gossip serving as manure and my mother's harsh words as water, this disease of love only continues to grow.
ai.modern: ஊராரின் அலர் பேச்சு எருவாகவும், அன்னையின் கடிந்துரைக்கும் சொல் நீராகவும் அமைய, இந்த காதல் நோய் மேலும் வளர்கிறது.
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the heroine uses a vivid agricultural metaphor to describe her love-sickness. The public gossip (கௌவை) of the townspeople acts as fertilizer or manure (எரு), while her mother's scolding words (அன்னை சொல்) act as water (நீர்). Instead of extinguishing or suppressing her passion, these external attempts to stop her love only nourish it, causing this affliction (நோய்) to grow even taller and stronger.

ai.literal: Saying 'we will extinguish fire with ghee' is like saying 'we will extinguish love by public rumor'.
ai.translation: To think that one can extinguish love through public gossip is like trying to put out a fire by pouring ghee on it.
ai.modern: நெய்யை ஊற்றி நெருப்பை அணைப்போம் என்று கூறுவது போலாகும், ஊரார் பேசும் வதந்தியைக் கொண்டு காதலை அடக்குவோம் என்று நினைப்பது.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses a vivid analogy to show how public gossip (கௌவை) only intensifies secret love (காமம்) instead of suppressing it. Ghee is highly inflammable, and pouring it on a fire (எரி) will only make the flames leap higher, not extinguish (நுதுப்பேம்) them. Similarly, when the townspeople gossip about the lovers, their talk acts as fuel, heightening the lovers' desire and making their bond even stronger. The poet highlights the futility of trying to control or end a deep passion through social pressure and rumors.

ai.literal: Public gossip to feel ashamed is it possible, 'Do not fear, guard yourself' he said, many people to feel ashamed when he abandoned?
ai.translation: When he, who once assured me 'Do not fear,' has abandoned me so heartlessly that even onlookers feel ashamed, is it possible for me to feel ashamed of this public gossip?
ai.modern: "அஞ்சாதே, உன்னைப் பாதுகாப்பேன்" என்று அன்று சொன்னவர், இன்று பலர் வெட்கப்படும்படியாக என்னை விட்டுப் பிரிந்து சென்ற பிறகு, இந்த ஊர் அலருக்கு (வதந்திக்கு) நான் அஞ்சுவது இயலுமா?
ai.explanation: The heroine laments her lover's departure. He had once comforted her with the words 'añcal ōmpu' (do not fear, guard yourself), promising never to leave her. Now, he has abandoned her so publicly and cruelly that even the townspeople ('palar') feel ashamed on her behalf. In such a desperate state of public abandonment, she asks if it is even possible ('olvatō') for her to feel embarrassed or shrink back in shame ('nāṇa') because of the town's gossip ('alar'). The gossip is nothing compared to the profound betrayal of his broken promise.

ai.literal: They themselves if they desire, will grant grace, the lover; I desiring, public rumor raises, this town.
ai.translation: My lover will grant his grace only when he himself desires it; yet, this town is raising the very public rumor that I desire.
ai.modern: காதலர் தாம் விரும்பினால் மட்டுமே வந்து அருள் செய்வார்; ஆனால், நான் விரும்புகின்ற அலரை (வதந்தியை) இந்த ஊர் எழுப்புகிறது.
ai.explanation: The heroine, separated from her lover, notes that her lover's return depends entirely on his own will. However, she finds comfort in the gossip spreading through her town. The word 'kauvai' refers to the public rumor or scandal about their secret love. She welcomes this gossip because it is exactly what she desires; the public pressure from the rumor will eventually compel her lover to return and marry her.
